skill.name: ddd-check-incremental
skill.description: Checks changed or new Java files in Git differences against DDD layer rules before commits.
skill.summary: Reviews changed Java files for focused DDD compliance issues.
skill.author: bookiosk

security_audit.summary: All 22 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code formatting. The only executable examples use fixed, read-only Git and grep commands without dynamic input, destructive behavior, or data transmission.

static_findings.snippet: Load only the rule files matching the changed layers. Plus always load `rules/anti-patterns.md`.
- [ ] 阻断型 throws exception, 分支型 returns ResultDO (see `references/exception-handling.md`)

content.user_title: Check Changed Java Code for DDD Compliance
content.value_statement: DDD violations in changed Java files can be missed before commits. This skill reviews Git differences by layer and reports focused fixes.
actual_capabilities: Lists staged, unstaged, or combined changed Java files from Git differences.
Classifies changed files into common, domain, application, adaptor, infrastructure, client, or model layers.
Checks structure, dependencies, naming, exception handling, and documented DDD anti-patterns.
Assigns critical, high, medium, or low severity to reported violations.
Reports file-specific problems, rule references, and suggested fixes.
limitations: Reviews only changed or new Java files, not the complete repository.
Depends on referenced rule files that are not included in this skill package.
Uses package paths and framework base classes specific to the documented project structure.
Performs instruction-guided review and does not compile code or run automated architecture tests.

use_cases.title: Review Before Commit
use_cases.description: Check staged Java changes for DDD violations and receive precise fixes before creating a commit.

use_cases.title: Assess Pull Request Changes
use_cases.description: Review modified layer boundaries and framework conventions without analyzing unchanged files.

use_cases.title: Enforce Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Apply shared DDD rules consistently during routine development and identify deviations early.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my staged Java changes for DDD compliance. Report only real violations and suggest exact fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Working Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all staged and unstaged Java changes. Classify each file by layer and cite the relevant rule for every violation.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Domain Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect changed domain Java files for forbidden dependencies, base-class errors, public setters, and exposed infrastructure concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Cross-Layer Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze changed Java files across all DDD layers. Explain dependency violations, severity, architectural impact, and the smallest compliant correction.

output_examples.input: Check the staged Java changes before I commit.
output_examples.output: DDD Check: 3 files changed. Order.java has a critical infrastructure dependency. Move persistence access behind GatewayI. Two other files have no reportable issues.

output_examples.input: Review my changed application and client files.
output: CreateOrderService.java: High. The command service does not extend ApplicationCmdService. Update the base class.
OrderDTO.java: High. A domain object is exposed through the DTO. Map it to client-safe fields.

best_practices: Run the check with a clean understanding of which staged and unstaged changes should be included.
Keep the referenced layer rules available and aligned with the repository architecture.
Verify each suggested fix against project requirements before committing.
anti_patterns: Do not use this incremental check as a replacement for a complete architecture audit.
Do not accept severity labels without reviewing the cited rule and source context.
Do not apply project-specific base-class rules to repositories that use another DDD framework.

faq.question: Which files does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews changed or new Java files reported by staged, unstaged, or combined Git differences.

faq.question: Does it review unchanged Java files?
faq.answer: No. The workflow is intentionally incremental and excludes unchanged files.

faq.question: Which DDD layers can it classify?
faq.answer: It recognizes common, domain, application, adaptor, infrastructure, client, and model package paths.

faq.question: What does a finding include?
faq.answer: A finding includes the affected file, severity, problem, relevant rule, and an exact suggested fix.

faq.question: Are the referenced rule files included?
faq.answer: No. The package contains only SKILL.md, so the repository must provide the referenced rules and exception-handling guidance.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source files?
faq.answer: No. Its documented workflow reads changed files and reports compliance issues without editing source code.
